title: Probabilistic Tenant Stitcher for Late-Arrival Metering and Confidence-based Reallocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a probabilistic tenant-stitching stage to the usage ingestion pipeline to handle out-of-order and late-arrival events from multiple telemetry sources (streaming ingress, batched logs, edge proxies). The component will generate a confidence score for tenant attribution and emit either an immediate attribution event or a conditional reallocation action for downstream billing jobs.
motivation: We continue to see 6-12% of daily token volume being un-attributed or mis-attributed due to out-of-order arrival and transient session IDs persisted only at the edge. These cases are causing billing skew, manual investigations, and support tickets. Deterministic heuristics (exact session id matches + strict time windows) miss many reconciliations. A probabilistic approach permits higher recall while surfacing attribution confidence to downstream systems and billing teams.
scope: Implement the stitcher as a self-contained Flink/Spark streaming stage deployed in the ingestion cluster. It will consume normalized events from the canonical ingestion topic, enrich with feature vectors (session hints, ip_hash, user_agent_fingerprint, route_hint), compute a match score against recent open-unattributed records, and emit attribution or reallocation messages. Include a backfill worker to run the same logic over a 90-day hot window for account reconciliation.
non_goals: This task does not change pricing rules or UI-facing invoices. We will not attempt to retroactively rebill customers within this ticket; billing adjustments will be surfaced as suggestions for the finance pipeline to ingest in a follow-up project.
technical_design:
- Input: canonical-ingest.v1 (normalized events) and orphan-index.v1 (recent unattributed candidates)
- Feature extraction: deterministic keys + hashed fingerprints + temporal decay weight
- Matching: lightweight logistic regression model producing a confidence score (0-100) implemented in Java for low-latency evaluation
- Thresholds: config-driven per-tenant thresholds; scores below soft-threshold -> mark as provisional (defer for 1h re-evaluation), scores above hard-threshold -> immediate attribution
- Outputs: attribution-events.v1 (final), provisional-attribution.v1 (for re-eval), reallocations.proposal.v1 (for finance backfill ingestion)
- Failure modes: if model evaluation fails, fallback to deterministic time-window join and emit with low confidence tag
- Backpressure: circuit-breaker that switches to deterministic mode when processing lag > 30s
acceptance_criteria:
- Stitcher is deployed to canary and processes canonical-ingest.v1 at sustained input of 10k rps with <200ms per-event added latency
- False positive rate on a labeled testset <= 2% and false negative rate improved by >= 30% vs current deterministic join
- Downstream billing pipeline consumes reallocation proposals and flags them in the finance dashboard
- End-to-end test harness exists that can replay 7 days of production traffic and validate attribution stability
data_migration_plan:
- Run backfill worker in dry-run mode for 7 days to produce a reconciliation report
- Share report with finance for approval
- After approval, toggle backfill mode to produce reallocation proposals for ingestion by billing adjustments job
- Keep both deterministic and probabilistic outputs in the ledger for 60 days for auditing
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy to canary with 1% of traffic and introduce provisional-attribution flag in console metrics
2) Monitor precision/recall on test harness and production-sampled labels for 48h
3) Increase traffic to 10% and run backfill dry-run for affected tenants
4) Full rollout and enable reallocation proposals for finance ingestion
5) Schedule post-rollout incident review after 72h
monitoring_and_observability:
- Grafana dashboards: stitcher-throughput, avg-match-score, provisional-rate, fallbacks-rate
- Alerts: provisional-rate > 5% sustained for 15m, avg-match-score drop of >= 10 points vs baseline, processing-lag > 30s
- Tracing: add trace spans to trace attribution decisions with feature vector snapshot for debugging
- Audit log: every final attribution must include source keys and confidence score persisted to cold storage
backward_compatibility: Outputs include a deterministic_legacy_tag to preserve historical downstream semantics. Billing consumer can opt-in to use probabilistic_attribution via feature flag. Until migration is complete, we write both attribution types to the ledger.
testing_strategy:
- Unit tests for feature extraction and model evaluation
- Integration tests in CI that spin up local Kafka + Flink and run synthetic arrival patterns (out-of-order, delayed windows)
- Labeled sample evaluation: hold out a 5-day set of production traffic labeled by SREs and run nightly scoring
- Chaos test: simulate broker partitioning and verify circuit-breaker fallback
